observation.visible_scene: A dimly lit, orange-hued miniature/stop-motion scene with dinosaur figures: a sail-backed theropod (Spinosaurus-like) on the right, a frilled quadruped (Triceratops-like) on the left, and a central creature head with an open, toothed jaw. A tall, billowing plume of pinkish-orange smoke or fibrous cloud fills the center of the frame, partially veiling the central head. The lighting stays consistently warm red-orange throughout.
visible_changes: The central smoke plume rises and expands upward over the sequence, its dense body shifting so that the open-mouthed head behind it becomes progressively more exposed (clearly visible from mid-segment onward).
Wispy tendrils at the top of the plume drift and curl upward, indicating continuous smoke motion rather than a static cloud.
The left and right dinosaur figures remain in fixed positions and poses throughout the excerpt; no limb or body movement is visible on them.
The central head's pose (open jaw) stays constant; its apparent visibility changes are due to the moving smoke in front of it, not head motion.
The overall framing and background positions do not shift, consistent with a static camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: What generates the smoke and whether it is rising from below or being emitted by the central creature.
Whether the scene begins or ends with the smoke fully obscuring or fully clearing the head (both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries).
Any motion of the dinosaur figures before or after this segment.
uncertain_details: Whether the slight variation in the head's clarity is purely smoke occlusion or includes minor model movement.
The exact material of the plume (smoke vs. cotton/fibers) is not determinable from the frames.
